subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` be allowed to physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files under the existing retention rules and report those counts in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The patch follows the existing cleanup architecture, but it intentionally affects retained session transcript artifacts and intersects broader archive-retention policy that automation should not accept on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept Archive-Retention Cleanup
options.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

options.title: Ask For Broader Upgrade Proof
options.body: Pause for a larger real-store or upgrade-style cleanup transcript if maintainers want more confidence before changing retained artifact behavior.

options.title: Defer To Archive Policy Work
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want the broader archive naming/no-delete policy resolved before cleanup starts removing these archives.

recommendation.title: Accept Archive-Retention Cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup command and maintenance UX boundary that this product decision changes.
